messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: realtime_p99_latency_us-west > SLO (p99=2.8s, target=2.0s). Triggered by monitoring rule 'realtime-p99-detect'. Paging SRE oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging Aisha (SRE) @Aisha — you are oncall for incidents in US regions.
Aisha (SRE): ack, I see the alert. Joining quick triage. starting checks — can someone drop the realtime dashboard link?
Tom (Infra): dashboard -> https://corp.redwood.dev/dashboards/realtime-latency?region=us-west . p95 jumped to ~700ms, p99 spike to 2.8s. Looks correlated with increased request tail size.
Priya (ML Eng): curious if KV cache miss rates spiked. Pulling cache metrics now.
Aisha (SRE): running quick kubectl to see pod restarts / OOMs in serving cluster (us-west-realtime):
```
kubectl -n realtime get pods -l app=realtime-serving -o wide
# all pods Ready 3/3, no restarts
```
Tom (Infra): infra-level looks healthy. No node CPU pressure. GPU util steady. Network egress slightly higher from a subset of nodes (10.2.3.x).
Priya (ML Eng): KV cache miss rate:
```
kv_cache_miss_rate{cluster="us-west"} = 18% (baseline 3%)
kv_cache_latencies p95=12ms p99=220ms
```
Priya (ML Eng): so large increase in misses + latency — could explain tail token cost and p99 blowup if many requests go to full compute path.
Aisha (SRE): any recent deploys / rollout?
Tom (Infra): deploy-bot: Rollout completed: realtime-serving v2026.03.14-rc -> prod at 4650001000 by deploy pipeline.
Aisha (SRE): ok there was a rollout ~2.5 min before alert. Priya, is the change likely to affect cache keying or prefix behavior?
Priya (ML Eng): checking diffs — the release added a small change to prompt hashing for cache keys to support structured tool-calling. Potential that some keys are not matching. I'm rolling back that small change on a canary to validate.
Ben (Customer Success): any customer impact? CS has flagged a small set of enterprise calls from partner 'NovaApps' showing high latency in their logs. They reported user-facing slowness.
Aisha (SRE): triage summary so far: p95 up modest, p99 severe; root cause hypothesis: KV cache miss regression from recent deploy causing compute path surge and tail latency. Customer impact: yes — some enterprise customers showing degraded UX.
Tom (Infra): mitigation options: 1) rollback the release (fast but broad), 2) force cache warm from historical prefixes, 3) route traffic to dedicated older model variant.
Priya (ML Eng): can we do targeted rollback for the cache key change only? I can push a patch to restore previous hashing behavior - that should be quick and low risk.
Aisha (SRE): do it. While Priya pushes, I'll create a temporary routing rule to prefer warm instances and reduce concurrency on cold ones.
Priya (ML Eng): patch pushed to canary at 4650001250. Observing metrics...
Tom (Infra): creating routing override: set policy 'prefer-warm' in us-west realtime pool.
Aisha (SRE): after canary patch p99 dropped to 1.9s within 30s on canary subset. Great sign. Rolling patch to rest of cluster now.
Priya (ML Eng): rollout to 80% at 4650001275. Monitoring cache miss rate: dropping to ~4% on patched nodes.
Ben (Customer Success): I'll reply to NovaApps with interim note: "We observed a transient service degradation; our oncall triage indicates a quick mitigation is underway; we'll follow up after full rollback."
Aisha (SRE): p99 back under SLO at 4650001290 (p99=1.7s). p95 stable ~600ms. Closing immediate paging. Next steps: postmortem, add unit test to prevent keying regressions, and add alert that watches cache-miss rate delta >10% over baseline.
oncall-bot: Incident resolved for paging rule 'realtime-p99-detect' at 4650001295.
Priya (ML Eng): filed PR for test: ensure cache key invariants + e2e that exercises tool-calling paths.
Tom (Infra): I'll add a temporary dashboard panel that correlates cache miss % with p99 to make future triage faster.
Aisha (SRE): thanks everyone. I'll open the incident ticket and assign owners for postmortem (Aisha lead, Priya root-cause, Tom infra mitigations, Ben customer comms). If anything else pops, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
